summary: The authors generated four BaxBench-derived backend services (image→GIF converter, credit-card store, process monitor, uptime checker) in three environments: JavaScript/Express via Bolt, Python/FastAPI via ChatGPT, and Rust/Actix via Gemini. After functional validation, each service ran under a 48-hour JMeter workload while OS-level memory, response time and throughput were recorded and tested for trends with Mann-Kendall/Sen's slope. Static analysis (CodeQL, Semgrep, LeakAudit, SlowQL plus Claude Code review subagents) and an exploratory comparison with three human-written Python GitHub projects round out the study.

claims.claim: Memory usage is the most consistent aging indicator: significant upward trends in 11 of 12 application-environment combinations.
claims.evidence: Table I and §V-A. Only Rust Image Converter is non-significant. Memory is total OS-level RAM, not process memory (Threats: monitoring granularity), and each combination is a single 48h run.

claims.claim: Response time and throughput degradation are heterogeneous across environments.
claims.evidence: §V-A/§V-B: JavaScript shows significant latency growth in 3 of 4 apps, Python in 1, and one Rust result is spike-dominated. Language, framework, generation platform and runtime are fully confounded (one implementation per cell).

claims.claim: Static analysis identifies plausible code-level aging mechanisms (unbounded persistent state, missing cleanup, subprocess retention).
claims.evidence: §V-C (RQ3). The mechanisms come mainly from an LLM-assisted multi-agent review whose precision is not validated. The authors admit the correspondence with runtime trends is not uniform.

claims.claim: Human-written implementations show comparable or stronger aging.
claims.evidence: §V-D, Table IV: three Python GitHub projects with all memory trends significant. They are not replicas (different libraries and architectures), and the authors label the comparison exploratory.

patterns.note: Passing BaxBench-derived functional tests did not reveal resource accumulation that appears under sustained load. A test-pass verifier is insufficient for long-running services, though the evidence is thin.
CodeQL/Semgrep/LeakAudit/SlowQL needed custom rules for aging faults and were supplemented by LLM review. Static findings were only partly consistent with runtime trends.
Uses a Claude Code multi-agent review (specialist + general + performance-engineering validator) with no accuracy validation.

methodology.sample: 4 scenarios × 3 environments = 12 generated apps, one implementation and one 48h run each, plus 3 human-written Python apps.
methodology.baselines: Exploratory comparison with non-equivalent human-written GitHub projects. No controlled baseline.
methodology.models: Bolt (JavaScript), ChatGPT 5.0 (Python), Gemini 3.0 (Rust), all via chat/web platforms. Platform and language are confounded.
methodology.variance: Single run per configuration. Mann-Kendall significance and Sen's slope with CIs on within-run time series, but no repeated independent runs (acknowledged).
methodology.ablations: None. Language, framework and generator are not separated.

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint. No venue in comment or journal_ref.
standards.artifacts: Replication package with data, source code and scripts at github.com/chas42/generated-software-llm (branch project-2026). Time-series plots are in the package annex.

biases.detail: 12 apps, one generation and one 48h run each.
Memory is measured at OS level, so trends may reflect OS caches or background activity rather than application leaks (acknowledged).
No repeated runs. Within-series trend tests do not capture run-to-run variability.
Aging mechanisms identified by Claude Code review agents without precision/recall checks.
Each language is tied to a single generator and framework, so no factor can be attributed. The contributions list also says Python/Flask while the setup says FastAPI.

coi.affiliations: Federal Rural University of Pernambuco (Brazil), University of Naples Federico II and Gran Sasso Science Institute (Italy).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Bolt, ChatGPT, Gemini as generators. Not evaluated favorably or unfavorably as products.
coi.detail: Academic authors with no vendor ties.

verdict_reason: The question of operational reliability beyond functional tests is a useful and under-studied one. The evidence is thin: 12 single-run apps, OS-level memory, fully confounded factors and unvalidated LLM review. Admit only as a caution signal, not as quantitative evidence.
applicability: Low to moderate. The transferable point for a backend team delivering healthcare-education content to front ends is that functional and contract tests on agent-generated services do not catch unbounded in-memory state, missing cleanup of temp files or subprocesses, or growing persistence. Agent-produced ingestion services should get a soak or load stage (and JVM heap/GC metrics, file-descriptor counts, and retention policies in specs) before release. Spec-driven templates could make retention and size limits explicit non-functional requirements. The study has no Java/JVM services, uses chat UIs rather than agent harnesses, and says nothing about multi-repo or mixed-host work.
